chunks: Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:

Regarding a camel driver who carries oil with him and says: it was lost, or spilled, or the road was cut off against him: "If he brings upright evidence against himself that the road was cut off against him or it was lost, then there is nothing upon him; otherwise, he is liable."

And regarding a man for whom another man carried food in his boat, then it decreased, he said: "He is liable." I said to him: "Perhaps it sometimes increased." He said: "Do you know that he added anything to it?" I said: "No." He said: "It is yours."

key_terms.الزَّيْتَ: oil being carried as entrusted property
key_terms.بِبَيِّنَةٍ عَادِلَةٍ: upright legal evidence establishing the claim
key_terms.جَمَّالٍ: a camel driver or transporter of goods
key_terms.سَفِينَتِهِ: his boat used for transporting goods
key_terms.ضَمِنَ: became liable to compensate for the loss

ai.seo_question: When is a transporter liable for goods that were lost, spilled, stolen, or reduced during transport in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings on liability for transported goods. A carrier is not liable if he establishes loss through upright evidence, but otherwise must compensate; likewise, when goods diminish in transport, the transporter is held liable unless there is proof of an added amount.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3920 - Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (as), regarding a camel driver who carries oil and claims that it was lost, spilled, or taken by robbers.
Imam (as) said: "If he brings trustworthy evidence that it was stolen, lost, or taken, then he is not liable. Otherwise, he is responsible for compensating it."
And regarding a man who transported food for another man in his boat, but the quantity decreased,
Imam (as) said: "He is liable."
I said to him: "Sometimes the quantity increases."
Imam (as) said: "Do you know that he added anything to it?"
I said: "No."
Imam (as) said: "Then it belongs to you."
